passage:
A singer posted an angry message online after reading a rude comment. Thousands of people saw it before she deleted it.
The next day, she wrote an apology. Some fans accepted it. Others said the apology was only written because she had been criticized.
In media class, students discussed the event. Their teacher asked them to separate three things: the mistake, the apology, and the change after the apology.
One student said, "A good apology should not be the end. It should be the start of different behavior."
The class learned that online words move quickly, but trust returns slowly. Deleting a post may remove words from a page, but not from people's memory.
